quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables (20.1) and for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard mechanics are present (prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-limited notice failure, and no adverse settlement without consent) (20.4), and 20.5 adds procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in addition to (not in place of) the defence obligation. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow — unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and Vendor instructions. Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so Vendor's indemnity is not squeezed by the liability cap (better than the fallback 3× super-cap). No redline required; separate concerns about the cap base in 21.1 belong to the limitation-of-liability rule.

quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.
rationale: The IP package meets our preferred position. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right to deliver the Services (and Section 15.1 bars sale, advertising use, commingling and model training). Section 14.2 gives Customer ownership of each Deliverable with an express Vendor assignment, personnel assignments and further-assurance covenant. Section 14.3 leaves Vendor with its pre-existing Vendor Technology but routes embedded Vendor Technology to the Section 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works for Customer's business. Section 14.4 excludes joint ownership absent a signed instrument identifying exploitation rights, and keeps feedback voluntary with Customer retaining unrestricted rights. Minor points noted only: ownership of Deliverables is conditioned on payment of Fees, and Vendor may process Customer material to "improve the Services for Customer" — both are within market norms and do not assign Customer IP or data, so no redline.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] As drafted the cap is measured by "Fees", which Section 1.5 defines as only the USD 12,000 one-time Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the mutual cap is effectively USD 12,000 and far below our floor of twelve months' charges. We have moved the cap to the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the preceding twelve months and USD 1,000,000; the Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) remain outside the cap as already drafted.

ops.newText: shall not exceed the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000
ops.oldText: shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim

proposal.summary: Replace the illusory cap base (Fees = USD 12,000 implementation fee under the first Order Form) with the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000.

quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: The structure of Section 21 is otherwise good: the cap is expressly mutual, indirect/consequential damages are mutually excluded (21.2), the Excluded Claims set in 21.3 covers confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and the other Party's IP, and Customer's payment obligation is carved out of "damages". The failure is the cap quantum: it is measured by "Fees", which Section 1.5 defines as only the "Implementation Fee", i.e. the one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form (Section 1.6), and is further narrowed to the first Order Form. Recurring subscription and service charges are therefore excluded, making the cap illusory at roughly USD 12,000 — far below the fallback of twelve months' fees and inside walk-away territory (cap below six months' fees). Minimal redline changes only the cap base in 21.1 to the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and USD 1,000,000; the existing carve-outs are left untouched.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position: Customer may assign without consent to an Affiliate or an M&A/asset-sale successor (24.1, notice only); Vendor may not assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a direct competitor (24.2); other assignments are subject to a mutual reasonable-consent standard (24.3); and our change of control gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service (24.4). No residual assignment or change-of-control language in § 30 or elsewhere cuts back these rights. No redline needed.

quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer, meeting the preferred position. Clause 12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer may engage any supplier and has given no exclusivity, non-compete, MFC or minimum-volume commitment, and clause 2.1 confirms there is no minimum quantity or purchase commitment and that declining to place further Order Forms is not a breach. Document-wide searches for "exclusive", "sole", and requirements-purchase language surface only unrelated uses (non-exclusive licence in 13, non-exclusive remedies in 19/21/30, exclusive jurisdiction in 28). Clause 12.4 restricts Vendor from marketing a competing analytics service — exclusivity running in Customer's favour, which the rule treats as acceptable and which we leave intact.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, and 15% of annual Fees per week of delay far exceeds any conceivable loss (and the remaining contract value). We have replaced it with customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, consistent with the dispute-withholding right in Section 7.3.

ops.newText: If any undisputed invoice is not paid within thirty days of its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month and the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until payment. Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar predetermined sum under this Agreement.
ops.oldText: If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment; replace with capped late-payment interest

quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by us (Customer) of 15% of annual Fees for every week an invoice is late — an uncapped, compounding sum that would rapidly exceed the remaining contract value and is triggered by a mere ten-day payment delay. That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (which contemplates only an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees). No other Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties appear in the document; termination (Section 9.4) and force majeure (Section 27) are penalty-free, and no SLA credit construct runs against us. Redline deletes the liquidated-damages mechanic and substitutes customary simple interest at 1% per month on undisputed overdue amounts, aligned with the dispute-withholding protection in Section 7.3.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.
rationale: Section 13 meets the preferred position on all material terms. The subscription grant in 13.1 expressly extends to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf (no written-notice condition required), plus Authorized Users. The paid-up grant in 13.2 is perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and fully paid, with contractor support rights. Clause 13.3 permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor via an assignment permitted by Section 24, and § 24.1 allows assignment to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent, with § 24.4 barring Vendor from terminating, repricing or suspending on our change of control. Revocation/suspension is confined to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity, so the licence is not revocable at will. The § 1.1 "Affiliate" definition is standard >50% control. No redline required.

quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction on us. Clause 12.3 expressly confirms the opposite: we remain free to develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product or service, engage any supplier, and do business in any field or territory, with an acknowledgement that we have given no exclusivity, non-compete, MFC, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. The only competitive covenant, clause 12.4 ("Vendor shall not develop or market a service that competes directly with Customer's proprietary analytics products during the term"), binds the Vendor and benefits us, so it is not flagged. Sweeps of §§ 2, 12, 13, 26 and 30 for "compete", "exclusiv", "field of use", "territor" and "restrict" surfaced no covenant limiting our business. This meets the preferred position (no restriction on Customer); no redline required.

quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
rationale: Section 9.4, read with Section 29.4 (thirty days' notice), gives Customer a convenience termination right over the whole Agreement or any Order Form on 30 days' written notice, with liability limited to accrued Fees and a refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (reinforced by Section 10 at p0045). There is no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the document, and no Vendor termination-for-convenience right — Vendor's termination rights are limited to material breach (9.1) and insolvency (9.2). This meets the preferred position in full; no redline needed.

quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
rationale: Section 22 is the only audit right binding us, and it meets the preferred position in full: frequency capped at once per twelve months (22.1), thirty days' prior written notice, normal business hours, off-site where practicable, conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds five percent (22.2), and an express bar on direct access to Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material and third-party confidential information. Section 23 contains no operative Vendor audit right, and no remote-monitoring or unannounced-inspection language appears elsewhere. Section 22.3 (findings as our Confidential Information, copy of the final report, shortfall payment resolving the issue) is additional protection in our favour. No redline required.

quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
rationale: Section 28 sets New York law (§28.1) and exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County (§28.2), which is exactly our preferred position. A document-wide search returns no arbitration provision, so there is no foreign-seated arbitration risk. The §28.2 carve-out for interim injunctive relief and the §28.3 executive escalation step are mutual and customary and do not displace the New York courts.

quote: 7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.
rationale: The single most-favoured-nation provision in the Agreement (§ 7.6) runs in our favour: Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than those offered to similarly situated customers. Searches for "no less favourable", "most favoured nation", "favourable", "parity", and "best terms", plus review of the pricing (§ 7), structure/scope (§ 2) and general (§ 30) sections, found no provision requiring Customer to extend Vendor its best terms or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer; Vendor-granted MFN pricing is welcome), so no redline is proposed.

quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position: § 2.1 expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment, confirms we pay only for Services ordered under an executed Order Form, and states that declining to place further orders is neither a breach nor a shortfall. This is reinforced by § 12 (p0051), where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment, and by § 7.1 (p0026), which bars any unstated minimum-use charge. No take-or-pay, committed spend, non-reducible seat count, or volume cap on our usage appears anywhere; the only "shortfall" concept is the licence-audit true-up in § 22, which is a usage reconciliation rather than a purchase commitment. § 8.2 also gives us a 30 days' non-renewal right on each Order Form, so no commitment persists without an exit.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: Searches for "solicit", "induce", "employ or engage", "hire", and "recruit" across the Agreement return no non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binding Customer; Sections 12, 16 and 30 (the likely homes for such language) contain none. To the contrary, Section 12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer has made no no-hire commitment and expressly preserves Customer's freedom to hire any person responding to general recruitment and to engage any supplier. This meets the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so no redline is warranted. Note that Section 12.4 imposes a limited competitive restriction on Vendor only, which runs in our favour and is not flagged.

quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
rationale: Renewal terms are twelve months (no multi-year auto-renewal), Customer alone can opt out on only thirty days' written notice (well inside our 30-day preferred maximum), and Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days beforehand, with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed. Clause 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. This meets the preferred position on every material term; the three-year initial term in 8.1 is a negotiated commercial term, not an auto-renewal issue.

quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position in full: six months of transition assistance on request (priced at the expiring Order Form rates, which is better for us than "then-current rates"), return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, and secure deletion with written officer certification thereafter. Two customer-favourable extras: Vendor may not withhold Customer Data over a fee dispute (p0048), and deletion is triggered only after we confirm successful return, with any law-required retained copy remaining protected (p0049). Section 10.1 preserves our Customer Data rights and expressly contemplates the transition period, so nothing conditions data return on payment. No redline required.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
rationale: Section 19 meets the preferred position on every material term: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel to industry standards (19.1); Deliverables materially conform to documentation and acceptance criteria for ninety days from the later of delivery or acceptance, and Hosted Services conform throughout the subscription term (19.2) — equal to or better than the preferred 90-day services / 12-month software benchmark; and 19.3 adds no-malicious-code and Applicable Law compliance warranties. The remedy in 19.4 is real: prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination of the affected item plus refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure, and it is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties, is mutual, and expressly states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy; Section 21 likewise preserves caps without cutting back the warranty (and 21.4 survives failure of an exclusive remedy). Minor points noted only, not deviations: the refund is measured by "Fees paid" rather than "paid or payable," and cure is owed "within a reasonable period" rather than a fixed cure window.

quote: 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
rationale: Section 18 meets the preferred position in full: Vendor must carry CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law (plus employer's liability of USD 1M), professional E&O of USD 2M, and cyber/privacy liability of USD 5M — appropriate given Vendor hosts and processes Customer Data under sections 15 and 17. Coverage runs through the term and for one year afterward, matching our model language. Clause 18.2 adds certificates of insurance on request, reputable insurers, primary coverage where customary, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and confirmation that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities — all favourable to us. No redline required.
